title: Tail-aware continuous-batching scheduler tuning for mixed prompt/response lengths
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Continuous batching currently uses a single-size-aware scheduler that underperforms on realistic traffic mixes where short prompts (<=64 tokens) and long prompts (>512 tokens) coexist. Symptoms: p95 latency regressions for short requests during load spikes, reduced GPU throughput due to frequent KV cache thrashing, and higher GPU memory fragmentation leading to OOMs on some nodes. Goal: Tune the continuous-batching scheduler and complimentary KV cache policies so short and long request tails are both satisfied — preserving low tail latency for short queries while keeping high token throughput for long sessions and minimizing peak GPU memory usage.
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency for short (<=64 tokens prompt, <=32 tokens generation) requests improves to <= 120ms under 3000 RPS mixed traffic
aggregate tokens/sec throughput for long sessions (>512 tokens) does not decrease by more than 8% compared to baseline
average GPU memory headroom increases by >= 12% on 24GB V100-equivalent nodes under our standard mixed workload
no production OOMs observed in 72h smoke test on canary cluster
automated regression test added: mixed-length synthetic workload run in CI with assertions for p50/p95/p99 and memory
progress_updates: 2026-03-05 - Ticket created by Aisha. Initial profiling attached. Observed that default batching window and single queue causes long requests to monopolize KV cache and increase per-request allocations.
2026-03-06 - Marcus ran baseline: baseline p95 short=210ms, long aggregate throughput=100k tokens/s, avg GPU mem available=1.8GB on 24GB instance. Attached perf-log-0306 and flamegraphs.

2026-03-07 - Implemented prototype 'tail-aware queue' that dynamically tags incoming requests into short/medium/long bins based on token-ahead estimate. Added fast-path for short bin with lower batch timeout and preemptive dispatch. PR draft: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/388 (WIP).

2026-03-09 - Experiment 1: tail-aware queue improved short p95 to 115ms at 2000 RPS but long throughput dropped 14%. Observed KV cache eviction frequency increased 30% due to interleaved long requests causing repeated cache growth and shrink cycles.

2026-03-10 - Added KV cache soft-partitioning: reserve lightweight slot quota for short sessions (configurable per runtime) and implement LRU within partitions. Memory accounting changes: track KV cache slices and report fragmentation. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/392.

2026-03-11 - Experiment 2: combined tail-aware queue + KV soft-partition reduces short p95 to 95ms and long throughput drop narrowed to 6%. GPU memory headroom improved by 9%. Still seeing periodic fragmentation after long bursty sessions.

2026-03-12 - Prototype kernel-level improvements: use pooled KV allocation with slab allocator to reduce fragmentation, and move KV slices for short sessions to a compact contiguous arena. Microbenchmarks indicate 18% fewer allocations and 22% lower peak RSS during synthetic long bursts. Added canary config flags and rollback switch.

Next steps: finish PR reviews, extend CI synthetic workload with GPU memory assertions, schedule canary rollout to runtime-canary-2 cluster on 2026-03-16, and monitor dashboard: dashboards/runtime/scheduler-mixed-length-2026.
decisions: Adopt tail-aware queueing (short/medium/long bins) as the default scheduling strategy behind a runtime flag for 1.19 rollout
Implement KV cache soft-partitioning with configurable quotas per tenant to protect short-path performance
Deploy slab-based KV allocation to reduce fragmentation instead of aggressive GC of KV entries
Expose two new runtime knobs in console: short_batch_timeout_ms and kv_short_quota_pct for customer tuning
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Long sessions may see slightly reduced throughput during high mix — mitigated by dynamic elasticity that relaxes short quota during low short-request load
Risk: New allocator could introduce subtle bugs — mitigation: exhaustive unit tests + shadow canary run for 7 days before enable-by-default
Risk: Additional complexity in billing/metrics — mitigation: add cost breakdown per queue in Console and document impact in runbook
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on KV accounting correctness and that short-path fast dispatch cannot starve medium-length requests completely. Look for memory-safety invariants in slab allocator code and ensure all new metrics have clear owner and dashboard panels.
